open_errors.issue: Meera recalls that Rohan asked about her mother 'the next night' after she turned her face to the wall. In ch 9 the question about her mother comes earlier that same night, before she sleeps and before the rope-end moment. The night after (ch 10) he only refuses questions about his coat.
open_errors.fix: Place his question about her mother earlier that same night.

patches.find: And he had not paid her back in coin or thanks. He had asked the right question the next night, a plain one, about her mother.
patches.replace: And he had not asked for coin or thanks. Earlier that night he had asked the right question, a plain one, about her mother.

open_errors.issue: Rohan's Salt Fox question is called 'the same question as three nights ago'. He last asked it on the winter line in ch 4, the night they were bound, about seven nights earlier. Three nights before ch 13 (ch 9) he chose to ask about her mother instead.
open_errors.fix: Point back to the ch 4 asking.

patches.find: It was the same question as three nights ago. He knew that, and so did she.
patches.replace: It was the same question he had asked on the winter line, the night they were bound. He knew that, and so did she.

open_errors.issue: On day 16 Rohan tells Kiran he has lived on Meera's mountain for 'twelve days'. Ch 20 already uses twelve days for day 12, and ch 23 has him say he has carried the rope fifteen days on day 17.
open_errors.fix: Replace the wrong count with a round figure that fits.

patches.find: And I have lived on your sister's mountain for twelve days, and I have been fed, and mended, and written in a book,
patches.replace: And I have lived on your sister's mountain for half a month, and I have been fed, and mended, and written in a book,

open_errors.issue: Rohan opens his seam with 'a knife she had not known he kept'. In ch 8 Meera watches him stir the sattu with his knife.
open_errors.fix: Make it the knife she has already seen.

patches.find: The seam gave to a knife she had not known he kept.
patches.replace: The seam gave to the small knife he had once stirred sattu with.

open_errors.issue: Varun sees Meera in 'a stained pattu with a hole in the hem'. The brown pattu with the hole in the hem is the one Rohan has been wearing since ch 21, and the soldiers strip it off him in this same chapter. Ch 27 confirms the hole is in his borrowed pattu.
open_errors.fix: Drop the hole from Meera's pattu.

patches.find: He was looking at Jassi's second, a woman in a stained pattu with a hole in the hem, and nothing more.
patches.replace: He was looking at Jassi's second, a woman in a stained and frayed pattu, and nothing more.

open_errors.issue: The stitches over the brass button are said to have been sewn 'ten winters back, so that nobody would find what lay under them'. In ch 1 Meera stitches this button, the token from the latest drop, into the spine on the morning the wardens arrive.
open_errors.fix: Keep the binding ten winters old, but have the button stitched in on the ch 1 morning.

patches.find: She had sewn them herself, ten winters back, so that nobody would find what lay under them unless he meant to take the book apart.
patches.replace: She had bound the book herself, ten winters back, and stitched the button under the binding the morning the wardens came, so that nobody would find it unless he meant to take the book apart.

open_errors.issue: The grey-bearded officer is said to have settled something 'in a lane the night before'. The torches at Ranu were on the night of day 18, the escape was at dawn of day 19, and the night walk was the night of day 19. The Fair is day 20, so the lane was two nights before.

patches.find: Then he stood beside it with his hands empty, as if he had settled something with himself in a lane the night before.
patches.replace: Then he stood beside it with his hands empty, as if he had settled something with himself in a lane two nights before.
